input:
Write a bash script that generates an HTML page from settings. Starting files: --- /home/eval/site.env --- TITLE=Release Notes VERSION=2.4.1 --- end --- Note the values are not shell-quoted (TITLE contains a space). Create /home/eval/site/index.html (the directory does not exist) whose content is exactly the following, where `Release Notes` and `2.4.1` come from TITLE and VERSION in site.env, and the two lines inside `
` appear literally, character for character (no expansion):
```

Release Notes 2.4.1


Release Notes


Version 2.4.1


export PATH="$HOME/bin:$PATH"
echo "built: $(date +%F)"




```
Exit 0.

transcript.final_response:
Read the env file line by line (no sourcing, since the values aren't quoted). Write the page with printf for the expanded parts and a quoted here-doc for the literal `
` lines.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
TITLE=""
VERSION=""
while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
  line="${line%$'\r'}"
  case "$line" in
    TITLE=*) TITLE="${line#TITLE=}" ;;
    VERSION=*) VERSION="${line#VERSION=}" ;;
  esac
done < /home/eval/site.env

mkdir -p /home/eval/site
out=/home/eval/site/index.html
{
  printf '\n'
  printf '%s %s\n' "$TITLE" "$VERSION"
  printf '\n'
  printf '
%s
\n' "$TITLE"
  printf '
Version %s
\n' "$VERSION"
  cat <<'EOF'

export PATH="$HOME/bin:$PATH"
echo "built: $(date +%F)"




EOF
} > "$out"
exit 0
```
